history.node: 17. Conjugacy and physical pairs — Search for hidden relationships
history.predecessor: 12. Fourier pairs — Change the representation, not the underlying information
history.question: Do observable physical pairings or complementarities reflect deeper symmetry analogous to mathematical conjugacy? (T-CONJUGACY, RD R12)
scene: Begin with a complex Fourier coefficient and its conjugate.
Then show how pairs of conjugate-frequency coefficients help produce a real-valued signal.
Once the mathematical relationship is established, introduce your broader question about physical pairs and whether observable relationships reflect deeper symmetry in nature.
The interface could let the visitor compare several kinds of pairing—mathematical conjugacy, reflection, and physical complementarity—and investigate which share formal properties.

source.statement: x̂(ω) = ∫x(t)e^{−iωt}dt. For x = u + iv: x̂(−ω) − conj x̂(ω) = 2i·v̂(−ω). For x ∈ L¹(ℝ): x̂(−ω) = conj x̂(ω) for every ω ⟺ v = 0 almost everywhere — the converse by the uniqueness theorem on L¹ (Zhou–Siadat Theorem 1.15, read), and independently for finite signals and finite Hermite expansions. Realness is exactly the property that forces the conjugacy
C: x ↦ conj x and C̃: X(ω) ↦ conj X(−ω) are antilinear involutions with F∘C = C̃∘F; real signals = Fix(C), Hermitian-symmetric spectra = Fix(C̃)
conjugate pair ⟺ equal magnitude AND opposite phase (where X ≠ 0); equal magnitude alone ((1+i)e^{−t²/2}) and opposite phase alone (e^{−(ω−1)²/2}e^{iω}) do not give a conjugate pair
X_k = Σx_n e^{−2πikn/N}; for real x: X_{(−k) mod N} = conj X_k; pairs k ↔ N − k
self-paired indices: k = 0 always, k = N/2 iff N even; there X_k is real (phase 0 or π) and the "pair" degenerates to a reality condition on one coefficient; continuous: ω = 0 only
x ↦ (X₀, …, X_⌊N/2⌋) is invertible over ℝ (N real numbers either way); the conjugate half carries no independent information
each pair (X_k, X_{N−k}) is one real oscillation (2/N)|X_k|cos(2πkn/N + arg X_k): one amplitude, one phase; the imaginary parts of the pair cancel identically (a cancellation zero)
for a generic complex-valued signal the symmetry need not hold: x = (1, i, 0, 0) gives X = (1 + i, 2, 1 − i, 0); e^{−t²/2}e^{it} (FB4c)
for a unitary character χ of an abelian group conj χ = χ⁻¹, so a real function has f̂(χ⁻¹) = conj f̂(χ): ℝ (ω ↦ −ω), ℤ_N (k ↦ N − k), ℝ² with η (P ↦ −P) — one structure

forcedBy: x = conj x (realness), and nothing weaker: the defect of the symmetry, x̂(−ω) − conj x̂(ω), is exactly 2i·v̂(−ω), where v = Im x, and v̂ ≡ 0 only for v = 0 a.e. (P17Fa; uniqueness on L¹, Zhou–Siadat Theorem 1.15; exact without imported theorems for finite signals, P17Lc, and finite Hermite expansions, P17Ld).

dispersion.statement: The PDE φ_tt − c²φ_xx + μ²c²φ = 0 (a parameter μ, units 1/length) has plane waves e^{i(kx − ωt)} exactly when ω² = c²k² + μ²c²; its symbol in the project convention is c²k² + μ²c² − ω² = −c²(q(P) − μ²), P = (ω/c, k)
Dimensions: [ω/c] = [k] = [mc/ħ] = L⁻¹, [mc²/ħ] = T⁻¹; ω, k angular (hν = ħω, p = h/λ = ħk)
With μ = mc/ħ: ω² = c²k² + m²c⁴/ħ² ⟺ (ω/c)² − k² = (mc/ħ)²
Convention: the physics positive-frequency wave e^{−iω₀t} sits at −ω₀ in x̂(ω) = ∫x e^{−iωt}dt; "positive frequency" is a convention-dependent label

(ω/c, k) is a pair of coordinates in a plane carrying the Lorentzian quadratic form q = η(P, P); boosts act on it as on (ct, x) because the phase η(P, X) is invariant. It is a relation in frequency-wavevector / energy-momentum variables, not physical spacetime

nulls.relation: q(P) = 0, P ≠ 0 (ω = ±ck, m = 0); ηP ≠ 0, so not a kernel vector
Jv = 0 ⟺ g(θ)v = 0 (a kernel vector of a semidefinite metric)

nulls.object: zero index on the massless cone
nulls.relation: P = 0: the constant mode (ω = 0, k = 0) — on the cone for m = 0, not on the shell for m > 0

nullLink: The spectral null P and the spacetime null ray are related only through η: the wave e^{−iη(P, X)} with P null has constant phase along the null ray parallel to P (P17Dd). They are not one kind of zero, and they are not the same object.

massive.statement: m > 0: q(P) = μ² is a hyperbola (1 + 1) with branches ω/c = ±√(k² + μ²); in 1 + 3 a two-sheeted hyperboloid

Proper orthochronous Lorentz boosts preserve each positive- or negative-energy mass-shell branch separately. Each branch is one SO⁺(1,1) orbit: the boost with tanh φ = ck/ω (= v_g/c) carries a positive-energy point to (μ, 0) and a negative-energy point to (−μ, 0). Not claimed for the full Lorentz group: time reversal S_t and −I preserve q and exchange the branches (P17La, P17Ca)
the branches are asymptotic to the null cone (ω − c|k| = μ²c²/(ω + c|k|) → 0) and tend to it as μ → 0 at fixed k
frequency gap: no real k for |ω| < μc (evanescent waves); min ω = μc = mc²/ħ at k = 0

Along the worldline associated with the same on-shell four-momentum, the free massive plane-wave phase accumulates at the invariant proper-time rate mc²/ħ, up to sign convention. — assumptions (P17Lb): a single free massive plane wave e^{−iη(P, X)}; P on the shell q(P) = (mc/ħ)²; the straight worldline X(τ) = X₀ + (cτ/μ)P of the same on-shell momentum, on which τ is proper time; the sign convention e^{−iη(P, X)} (the opposite convention reverses the sign). On another worldline the rate differs (lab frame: ω). m = 0: the phase is constant along the light ray. This establishes a proper-time phase rate. It does NOT by itself establish that mass and proper time are Fourier-conjugate variables.

mass selects the level: Mass labels/selects the invariant level of the same Lorentzian quadratic form. m = 0 ⇒ q(P) = 0 (the null level); m > 0 ⇒ q(P) = (mc/ħ)² > 0 (a nonzero timelike mass-shell level). The form and the group SO⁺(1,1) are the same for every m; μ = mc/ħ labels the invariant level as r labels a rotation orbit (#14 chart: Kᵀη + ηK = 0, JᵀI + IJ = 0); μ is not a form parameter like c

massAnswer: Does mass appear as a parameter selecting a non-null level set of the same quadratic form whose m=0 case is null? Yes, exactly: Mass labels/selects the invariant level of the same Lorentzian quadratic form. m = 0 ⇒ q(P) = 0 (the null level); m > 0 ⇒ q(P) = (mc/ħ)² > 0 (a nonzero timelike mass-shell level). The form q = (ω/c)² − k² and the group acting on it are the same for every m; m does not change the geometry, it selects the level (P17Db, P17Dc, P17De, P17Lg). Consequences of the selected level (derived): a frequency gap at mc²/ħ, a rest frame, and the proper-time phase rate stated below. This does not say that mass is a wave.

posNeg.math: Mathematical Fourier redundancy: the same theorem in two variables. A real field has φ̃(−ω, −k) = conj φ̃(ω, k), i.e. b(k) = conj a(−k) (P17Rb, P17Rc). The partner of (ω, k) is (−ω, −k), not (−ω, k) (P17Rd).
posNeg.condition: It follows from the field being real, and only then: the equation admits complex solutions (P17Re); the reality pairing is available because the operator commutes with conjugation (P17Ra); for iψ_t + αψ_xx = 0 it is not (P17Rf, a PDE contrast only).
posNeg.physical: Physical mode interpretation (classical): a real field's negative-frequency part is fixed by its positive-frequency part; together they make one set of real oscillations. Which half is called positive depends on the sign convention (P17Db, P17Ce).
posNeg.quantum: Quantum particle/antiparticle interpretation: NOT USED. It needs a specific field theory and is recorded as a future branch.
posNeg.answer: For a real classical field the space-time spectrum satisfies φ̃(−ω, −k) = conj φ̃(ω, k): the reality condition pairs the mode at P = (ω/c, k) with the mode at −P, which lies on the same level set of q and on the other branch.

words.realField: For a real classical field the space-time spectrum satisfies φ̃(−ω, −k) = conj φ̃(ω, k): the reality condition pairs the mode at P = (ω/c, k) with the mode at −P, which lies on the same level set of q and on the other branch.
words.massLevel: In the spectral variables P = (ω/c, k) the dispersion relation is the level set q(P) = (mc/ħ)² of the Lorentzian form q = (ω/c)² − k²: m = 0 selects the null level, m > 0 a non-null level whose branches are single boost orbits, with mc/ħ the orbit invariant.
words.kinds: Seven kinds of pairing are kept apart: conjugacy, sign symmetry, orbit symmetry, reality constraint, independent physical states, notation-dependent pairing, and Fourier duality.
words.restClock: Along the group worldline of any mode on the mass shell the phase advances at mc²/ħ per unit proper time, so the rest frequency mc²/ħ and proper time τ are a Fourier-dual pair; this is duality, not complex conjugacy.
words.boost: Proper orthochronous Lorentz boosts preserve each positive- or negative-energy mass-shell branch separately.
words.level: Mass labels/selects the invariant level of the same Lorentzian quadratic form.
words.levels: m = 0 ⇒ q(P) = 0 (the null level); m > 0 ⇒ q(P) = (mc/ħ)² > 0 (a nonzero timelike mass-shell level).
words.phaseRate: Along the worldline associated with the same on-shell four-momentum, the free massive plane-wave phase accumulates at the invariant proper-time rate mc²/ħ, up to sign convention.
words.notDual: This establishes a proper-time phase rate. It does NOT by itself establish that mass and proper time are Fourier-conjugate variables.
words.spectralQ: Is there a physically meaningful formulation in which mass/rest energy acts as a genuine spectral variable conjugate to proper time?

converse.statement: for x ∈ L¹(ℝ): x̂(−ω) = conj x̂(ω) for every ω ⟺ x is real almost everywhere
converse.forward: x real ⇒ Hermitian symmetry: the identity x̂(−ω) − conj x̂(ω) = 2i·v̂(−ω), v = Im x (P17Fa)
converse.converse: Hermitian symmetry ⇒ x real a.e.: with y = conj x, ŷ(ω) = conj x̂(−ω) (P17Le), so ŷ = x̂ and the uniqueness theorem on L¹ gives y = x a.e. — Zhou and Siadat, Notes on Harmonic Analysis I (arXiv:1709.03377), Theorem 1.15: "If f ∈ L1 (R) and fˆ = 0 everywhere (fˆ is always continuous), then f = 0 a.e." (full text read; research/sources/zhou_siadat_2017.md)
converse.independent: proved exactly without importing any theorem: finite signals, every N (P17Lc: F F* = N·I; a Hermitian-symmetric X has a real inverse); finite Hermite expansions (P17Ld: the defect has h_n-coefficient 2i√(2π)iⁿ·Im c_n); and, given the inversion theorem (x, x̂ ∈ L¹), the imaginary part of the inversion integral has an odd integrand (P17Le)
